summary: SAML XML canonicalization strips namespace prefixes from idp:Assertion, causing tenant resolution failures in private deploy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after an IdP configuration change, service account and tenant resolution fail intermittently. Impact: NimbusPay's scheduled workers and admin console logins return 403/tenant-not-found errors, blocking daily batch imports. Environment: Private deployment in eu-west, identity-proxy v2.13.1 behind on-prem ingress. Observed behaviour: IdP-sent SAML assertions are accepted but Redwood's tenant lookup fails because the assertion's namespace prefixes are missing after canonicalization. Expected behaviour: Canonicalization should preserve the element namespace context needed for tenant mapping (e.g., idp:Assertion -> Assertion with the same namespace resolved).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) IdP sends SAMLResponse with prefixed namespace declarations (e.g., xmlns:idp="urn:example:idp") and attributes in idp:Assertion.
2) Identity-proxy receives POST to /saml/acs and forwards canonicalized XML to tenant-resolution service.
3) Tenant-resolution looks for namespaced Assertion/AttributeContext entries; lookup returns empty when prefixes are stripped.
4) Result: user maps to no tenant -> platform returns 403 with 'tenant not resolved' in logs.
logs:

comments: 2026-03-10 09:42 - Customer (Lena Ortiz): After we rotated our IdP metadata the next morning, scheduled workers failed with 403s. We reverted rotation and failures stopped — happy to provide samples.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks Lena — can you attach a base64 SAMLResponse and the IdP metadata? We'll triage. SLA first response: 2026-03-12.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Customer (Lena Ortiz): Uploaded SAMLResponse and IdP metadata to secure upload link.
2026-03-10 14:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Identified canonicalization output that has no namespace prefixes. Escalating to identity-proxy team. Assigned to Miguel Santos.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Eng (Miguel Santos): Reproduced in staging by sending an assertion with prefixed namespaces. C14N step in our XML library removes prefix tokens but keeps default namespace, and our tenant extractor expects the prefixed path (idp:Assertion). Working on a compatibility patch.
2026-03-11 15:50 - SRE (Ravi Khanna): In private cluster we observed matching error bursts coinciding with IdP metadata refresh events. No CPU/memory OOMs.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Our canonicalization routine (libxml2 based wrapper) normalizes XML by removing prefixes when a default xmlns is present, altering XPath expressions used by tenant-resolver.

Repro: Created minimal SAMLResponse with xmlns:idp and observed post-c14n payload contains 'Assertion' elements without the idp prefix but with default namespace; our tenant extractor uses namespaced XPath (e.g. //idp:Assertion/idp:Attribute[@Name='tenant']/text()).

Temporary mitigation tested: Updated tenant-resolver to evaluate namespace-agnostic XPath (local-name()='Assertion') and validated tenant resolution for provided samples in staging, but change is broader than desired without unit tests.
Logs/links: identity-proxy debug trace uploaded to s3://redwood-support/nimbuspay/; reproducible test available as pytest in PR #2712.
resolution: Workaround: Applied a hotpatch to tenant-resolver on NimbusPay's private control plane to use namespace-agnostic lookups (rolled at 2026-03-12 01:10 UTC). This restored scheduled workers and admin logins for the customer. Root cause: XML C14N step removed namespace prefixes when IdP supplied a default xmlns alongside prefixed declarations; our extractor relied on prefix-qualified XPath. Fix plan: 1) Merge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/2712 to make tenant-extraction tolerant of both prefixed and default-namespace assertions (target release v2.13.3). 2) Add unit tests for a variety of IdP metadata shapes and update runbook. 3) Offer NimbusPay a permanent config change option (identity-proxy flag) to enable namespace-agnostic lookups or map prefix tokens in their IdP metadata. Follow-up: Postmortem scheduled; security review of SAML handling to ensure no unintended escalation of identity claims.
